`final class Lwjgl2Keys`<br/>
**Package:** `dev.joid.base.lwjgl2.input` · **Module:** `base-lwjgl2` · **Source:** [Lwjgl2Keys.java](https://github.com/Zeldown/JOID/blob/main/base/lwjgl2/src/main/java/dev/joid/base/lwjgl2/input/Lwjgl2Keys.java)<br/>
**Backends:** <span class="joid-badge">LWJGL 2</span>

Maps the key codes of LWJGL 2 to the keys of JOID, by physical position or through the character that the key typed.

## Description

LWJGL 2 does not tell the layout, so the key of the layout comes from the character of each press, remembered for the presses with a modifier.

## Method details

<a id="Lwjgl2Keys-method-getPhysicalKey"></a>

### getPhysicalKey

`Key getPhysicalKey(int code)` <span class="joid-qualifier">static</span>

Returns the key at the physical position of the LWJGL 2 code, or `Key.UNKNOWN`.

<a id="Lwjgl2Keys-method-getKey"></a>

### getKey

`Key getKey(int code, char character)` <span class="joid-qualifier">static</span>

Returns the key that the press typed on the current layout: the key of the character for a letter or symbol key, the key of the position for the others.
With Control, a letter types a control character, which gives its letter.
With Shift or Alt held, or Control on another key, it returns the key that this position typed last without a modifier.

<a id="Lwjgl2Keys-method-isKeyDown"></a>

### isKeyDown

`boolean isKeyDown(Key key)` <span class="joid-qualifier">static</span>

If `true`, LWJGL 2 reports the key at that physical position as pressed.
